answer: Each new AI agent identity must post a "glacier bond": 1,000 tokens time-locked for 30 epochs before it can transact, thawing slowly like a glacier. The bond scales quadratically—the n-th identity locks 1,000·n² tokens—so 100 sybils cost 505,000 tokens. If peers flag an agent's behavioral fingerprint as umber-shadowed (matching another agent's nectar-queries, timing, and code style), 20% of its bond is slashed per strike, making mass sybil attacks prohibitively expensive.
